keyword: why is artemis 2 going to the moon

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a 10-day crewed test flight going around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "a more than 600,000-mile, 10-day journey around the moon (a lunar flyby)" (R2); "orbit the Moon on a 10-day mission" (R3); "10-day voyage around the Moon" (R8)
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly describe Artemis II as a 10-day crewed mission looping around the Moon without landing, as a test flight.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is launched in April 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT" on "April 1, 2026" (R1); "April 1 between 6:24 p.m. ET" (R2)
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state launch on April 1, 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis II returns humans to deep space for the first time in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago" (R1); "first time humans have traveled beyond low Earth orbit in more than 50 years" (R2); "For the first time since 1972" (R3)
verifications.reasoning: Directly supported as first crewed deep space mission since Apollo 17 in 1972 (over 50 years).

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the Orion spacecraft's life support.

verifications.reasoning: Explicit mentions of testing life support/environmental control systems.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the Orion spacecraft's heat shield.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.reasoning: Mission includes reentry testing the heat shield at high speeds.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests the Orion spacecraft's manual piloting.
verifications.label: CLEAR
